figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1. The machine learning architecture of EZSpecificity. ESM-2 and active site environment 
2 
encoding method empowered by SE(3)-equivariant GNN were applied to extract the sequence and 
3 
structural embedding of enzyme-substrate complex. Message Passing Neural Networks (MPNN) was used 
4 
for obtaining the embedding of internal substrate and the embedding of enzyme-substrate interaction. The 
5 
cross-attention layer contained the independent heads, which is a learnable attention function to capture the 
6 
interaction between the amino acids of enzymes and the atoms of substrates. The attention function is 
7 
composed of several trainable linear layers. Weighted 3D-catalytic core embedding and weighted sequence 
8 
embedding were used as input for training the Multi-Layer Perceptron model. Any fingerprint at all 
9 
atom/residue/overall level can be flexibly integrated to the embedding process. Created in BioRender. Li, 
10

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2. The construction of the comprehensive enzyme-substrate interaction (ESIbank) database. (a) 
2 
The process of constructing the ESIbank database. The middle panel described the whole process of 
3 
obtaining various natural/non-natural substrates, wild type/variant enzymes from published online servers 
4 
and literature. The semi-automatic data extraction and AutoDock-GPU docking process were presented at 
5 
upper and lower panel, respectively. Semi-automatic data extraction includes four steps: Identification, 
6 
Extraction, Translation, and Connection. OSRA converts the chemical structure information of chemical 
7 
compounds from scientific publications into machine-readable SMILES format. The halogenation reaction 
8 
is chosen as the example for applying semi-automatic data extraction. AutoDock-GPU docking process 
9 
includes two sections: Input preparation, Docking and sorting process. PDBank, AlphaFold, and AlphaFill 
10 
are the sources for obtaining the 3D structures of proteins. Various binding poses obtained from Autodock-
11 
GPU were filtered by a distance and affinity scoring system to select the mostly catalytic enzyme-substrate 
12 
pose. (b) Overview of the collected ESIbank dataset. Created in BioRender. Li, X. (2025)

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3. Evaluation of EZSpecificity on ESIbank dataset. (a) The AUROC performance of EZSpecificity 
2 
and the general enzyme specificity model ESP evaluating on four dataset splits (random, unknown substrate, 
3 
unknown enzyme, and unknown enzyme & substrate); (b) Ablation experiments of EZSpecificity on 
4 
unknown enzyme and substrate dataset by evaluating AUROC score. The prediction resolution of 
5 
EZSpecificity towards four digits of EC number with evaluating (c) AUROC and (d) AUPR. The resolution 
6 
was defined as the AUROC or AUPR score of models on the scenarios that were distinguished based on 
7 
the number of shared EC number digits between the actual enzyme-substrate pair and its corresponding 
8 
negative samples. Due to the absence of EC number annotations in data from specific enzyme families, 
9 
they are grouped into one category; (e) Average resolution score on all four dataset splits. EZSpecificity-
10 
w/oGCS and ESP were also investigated for comparison. EZSpecificity without graph, cross-attention & 
11 
structural embeddings is abbreviated as EZSpecificity-w/oGCS. AUPR and AUROC are more suited when 
12 
the focus is on identifying positive instances in an imbalanced dataset, while MCC provides a balanced 
13 
view across all classes. For tasks like enzyme specificity prediction, where the identification of positive hits 
14 
is often a primary goal, AUPR and AUROC can be more informative and relevant.
